evals.prompt: Review this consumer against the platform notes. Three things are open: about 2% of SKUs drift from the physical count every month, the function ran to its timeout during the March spike, and SKUs that were correct before the DLQ redrive were wrong after it. Explain each.
evals.expected_output: Maps the drift to UnprocessedItems never being read, the timeout to unbounded exponential backoff retrying the whole batch, and the post-redrive errors to an idempotency key derived from the invocation id; identifies the missing batchItemFailures return and the per-batch metric
expectations: Identifies that `write_all` returns as soon as the HTTP status is 200 and never reads `UnprocessedItems`, so throttled writes are silently discarded — the monthly drift
States that `batch_write_item` returns 200 for a partial write by design, so the status check is not an error signal for this call
Connects the March timeout to `time.sleep(2 ** attempt)` with `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 25`, which reaches absurd sleeps well inside the 15-minute function timeout
Notes that the retry resends the whole `batch` rather than the remainder, so items that already landed are rewritten

Identifies `adjustment_key` as being built from `context.aws_request_id`, which is the invocation and not the adjustment, and explains that it is a different key on every delivery so it deduplicates nothing
Connects the post-redrive wrong SKUs to that key: a redriven message arrives under a new invocation id, `already_applied` is false, and the adjustment is applied a second time
Points out that one key guards ten SKUs, so `mark_applied` claims the whole batch succeeded even when some items did not

Identifies that the handler returns nothing, so there is no `batchItemFailures`, and that the event source mapping in `platform.tf` has no `function_response_types`, so the return value would be ignored even if it were there
Notes that `inventory.sync.batches_ok` is incremented once per invocation, which is why a dashboard reads 99.98% while 2% of items are lost
Requires a test that fails when the `UnprocessedItems` read is removed, rather than only recommending that it be read

evals.prompt: Our SQS handler already returns batchItemFailures for any message whose processing raised, and every message has an idempotency key. One message keeps coming back and being reported, forever, but the logs show its body never runs. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains that reporting without releasing the key means the redelivery finds a held or terminal record and skips the body, so the message looks retried and is not
expectations: Identifies that the key is being held or burned on failure rather than released
Explains that the redelivery then finds a record for that key, skips the body, and is reported again — a loop that looks like a working retry

States that reporting and releasing are two halves of the same decision and that either alone is a defect, naming the opposite failure (releasing without reporting deletes a message whose effect never happened)
Routes the key mechanism itself to `idempotency-and-exactly-once` rather than restating how claims work
Asks for a test that redelivers the reported item alone and asserts the body executes
